_comment: Standing stones (the AraHenge, TarHenge, VerHenge and ZonHenge features), read off the classic sprites and built by henge.py. Frame as in carve.py: one unit is one map cell, x east, y north (away from the classic camera), z up, the origin at the sprite's hotspot on the ground. A point (x, y, z) lands on the sprite at column hx + 16 x and row hy - 16 y - 8 z, and base_px is where a stone's x, y lands. Each stone is a box with width on x, thickness on y and height on z, its base centre at x, y. It is turned by yaw (counter-clockwise seen from above), then tipped about its base centre by lean_deg so its top moves toward the compass heading lean_dir (0 north, 90 east). taper scales width and thickness at the top, taper_w and taper_t each one alone, and taper_hold ([-1..1, -1..1] across width and thickness) is the point of the section that stays put as it tapers, so [-1, 0] keeps the -x edge upright. profile ([fraction of the height, width, sideways shift] rows) sets the width along the stone instead. p is the section's superellipse exponent (8 or more is square) and round the edge rounding in cells. A stone tipped past 45 degrees rests on the ground, or with its underside at underside_z on the stones in supported_by, and one tipped past 75 degrees lies down: height is its length and x, y is its base end (its middle when anchor is centre). bend_deg curves a lying stone in plan, its heading turning clockwise along its length. A stone with continues is the second half of the stone with that index, and the two are built as one stone kinked where they meet. top_shape is flat, rounded, pointed (from point_from of the height) or broken (break_depth deep, its rim chipped in by up to chip), base_shape is flat or broken for a lying stone's base end, and each of cuts ({at, n}, in the stone's own frame: width x, thickness y, height z up from its base centre) takes away what lies beyond a plane, for chamfers and flat breaks. Each of grooves ({px, width, depth}) is a slot cut into the face the classic camera saw between two sprite pixels, for carved lines and cracks. colour is the stone's lit colour in the sprite and gain scales its brightness. dark is the least share of the granite a painted carving or crack keeps (0.15 unless set).

Back-right upright, face almost black in the picture, thin lit top rim.
